summary: Verified guardrail feature (fixes for 'when I push scout it keeps pausing'). Backend: all 4 new pytest cases pass — /api/bot/state exposes guardrail_status (null under defaults with total_spent=0), POST /api/bot/guardrails with total_spend_cap_sol=0 makes guardrail_status='total spend cap hit (0.000◎)', POST /api/bot/reset_spend zeroes spent_today_sol/loss_today_sol/total_spent_sol and returns {ok:true}, and restoring cap to 0.3 with reset spend returns guardrail_status back to null. Frontend: PAPER SCOUT starts running and stays running across 12s of 2s polling (does NOT auto-pause) — confirms the user's original bug is resolved for the paper case. REAL mode with tune-cap=0 + SAVE STRATEGY triggers the yellow guardrail-banner, and clicking SCOUT in that tripped state keeps running=false (frontend guard prevents starting; state confirmed via /api/bot/state). banner-reset-spend fires a 'Spend & loss counters reset' toast and zeroes counters. After restoring cap=0.3 + SAVE STRATEGY (+ /api/bot/reset_spend), the banner disappears and guardrail_status=null.

ui_bugs.issue: The toast.error('Can't start scouting') on tripped-guardrail SCOUT click was not captured by DOM query 2s after click. Functionality is correct (bot stays paused; scout_stayed_paused=true), but the toast either auto-dismissed quickly or got batched with the prior 'Strategy & limits saved' toast. Consider increasing toast duration or adding data-testid to critical toasts for reliable observability.

action_items: (Optional, LOW) Add data-testid to sonner toast root or increase duration for critical block toasts so E2E tests can reliably observe them.

(Nice-to-have) StrategyPanel.save() saves strategy + guardrails together (verified: setting tune-cap=0 and clicking SAVE STRATEGY did trip the backend guardrail_status). This is correct behavior but not documented — worth a code comment.
critical_code_review_comments: engine.guardrail_block() uses '>=' so a total_spend_cap_sol of 0 with total_spent=0 is considered tripped. That is what enables the safe REAL-mode UX test but also means a user who deliberately sets cap=0 as a kill-switch will see 'total spend cap hit (0.000◎)' — reason text could be friendlier for cap==0 (e.g. 'spend cap set to 0 — cannot buy').

In tick_real() the auto-pause path logs 'GUARDRAIL: … auto-paused' to decisions — good user visibility. However this only fires when tick_real() runs (every 6s). The onToggle frontend guard handles the same case on the client immediately — good redundant defense.

server.py POST /api/bot/reset_spend returns only {ok:true}, no updated state. Frontend has to re-poll to see the change. Consider returning fresh spent_today_sol/total_spent_sol for immediate UI feedback (minor).

rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: user pressed SCOUT in REAL mode and the bot instantly re-paused with no explanation. Root cause: engine.tick_real() checks guardrail_block() every 6s and auto-pauses if total_spent_sol >= total_spend_cap_sol (previously default 0.5 SOL, now 0.3). After cumulative real buys crossed the cap, hitting SCOUT would flip running=true, and within one tick tick_real() would auto-pause again. Fix (verified working): (1) /api/bot/state now returns guardrail_status so UI knows a guardrail is tripped; (2) POST /api/bot/reset_spend zeroes counters; (3) onToggle in App.js checks st.guardrail_status BEFORE calling toggle and shows an explanatory error toast, preventing the flip-then-pause cycle; (4) guardrail-banner + banner-reset-spend button give the user an in-context recovery path. Reproduction: set cap=0.01, run bot briefly in real mode, then observe SCOUT no longer flips running=true — instead a toast explains and the banner surfaces reset.
